## Production

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=One_Hundred_Years_of_Solitude_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Production")]

### Development

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=One_Hundred_Years_of_Solitude_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Development")]

[Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") acquired the rights to *[One Hundred Years of Solitude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Hundred_Years_of_Solitude "One Hundred Years of Solitude")* in March 2019.[[2]](#cite_note-2) Before his death in 2014, author [Gabriel García Márquez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gabriel_García_Márquez "Gabriel García Márquez") had refused to sell the rights to the novel as he did not believe the time constraints of a feature film were sufficient for a proper adaptation.[[3]](#cite_note-3)[[4]](#cite_note-4) The series was filmed with the support of García Márquez's family, who requested that it be shot in Colombia, in Spanish, and with Colombian actors.[[5]](#cite_note-5) The producers scouted several locations for filming, including [Cali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cali "Cali"), [Villavicencio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villavicencio "Villavicencio"), [Girardot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Girardot,_Cundinamarca "Girardot, Cundinamarca"), [Palomino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palomino,_Colombia "Palomino, Colombia"), [Santa Marta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Marta "Santa Marta"), and [Barranquilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barranquilla "Barranquilla").[[6]](#cite_note-Guzmán-2024-6)

> As a filmmaker, as a Colombian, it has been an honor and an enormous challenge to work on a project of the complexity and responsibility of *One Hundred Years of Solitude*, always trying to understand the difference between literary and audiovisual language, to be able to construct images that contain something of the beauty, poetry and depth of a work that has impacted the entire world. We have done it with love and respect for the novel, with the help of an exceptional technical and human team.

— Director [Laura Mora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Mora "Laura Mora")[[7]](#cite_note-7)

### Casting

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=One_Hundred_Years_of_Solitude_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Casting")]

The cast was chosen through an open casting call in 2022.[[8]](#cite_note-8) The casting team saw more than 10,000 candidates for the 25 main roles.[[9]](#cite_note-Clarke-2024-9) Only 30% of the cast were professional actors.[[10]](#cite_note-10) In addition to the main cast, 20,000 extras were selected.[[11]](#cite_note-11) The cast was partially leaked on 26 April 2023.[[12]](#cite_note-12)

### Filming

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=One_Hundred_Years_of_Solitude_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Filming")]

Principal photography on the first part of the series took place from May to December 2023.[[13]](#cite_note-Kay-2024-13) The series was filmed entirely in Colombia,[[14]](#cite_note-14)[[15]](#cite_note-15) specifically in [La Guajira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Guajira_Department "La Guajira Department"), [Magdalena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magdalena_Department "Magdalena Department"), [Cesar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cesar_Department "Cesar Department"), [Cundinamarca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cundinamarca_Department "Cundinamarca Department"), and [Tolima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tolima_Department "Tolima Department").[[16]](#cite_note-16) The fictional town of [Macondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macondo "Macondo") was built near [Alvarado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alvarado,_Tolima "Alvarado, Tolima") by 1,100 workers.[[6]](#cite_note-Guzmán-2024-6) Four versions of the town were built to depict the passage of time.[[13]](#cite_note-Kay-2024-13) The producers purchased furniture from local antique stores and had fabrics and artifacts made by local artisans for the sets.[[9]](#cite_note-Clarke-2024-9) Filming required a crew of nearly 600 people, all from Colombia.[[17]](#cite_note-17) Netflix reported that series' production generated 225 billion [COP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombian_peso "Colombian peso") ($51.8 million USD) for Colombia's economy.[[18]](#cite_note-18)

Production on the second part of the series began in February 2025.[[19]](#cite_note-19)

## Release

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=One_Hundred_Years_of_Solitude_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Release")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/be/Stand_de_la_serie_%22Cien_a%C3%B1os_de_soledad%22.jpg/250px-Stand_de_la_serie_%22Cien_a%C3%B1os_de_soledad%22.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Stand_de_la_serie_)

A promotional display for the series at the [Guadalajara International Book Fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guadalajara_International_Book_Fair "Guadalajara International Book Fair") in December 2024

A teaser trailer for the first season was released on 17 April 2024.[[20]](#cite_note-20)[[21]](#cite_note-21) Promotional stills were released on 18 October.[[9]](#cite_note-Clarke-2024-9) The first two episodes premiered at the [Círculo de Bellas Artes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Círculo_de_Bellas_Artes "Círculo de Bellas Artes") in [Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid "Madrid") on 22 November 2024.[[22]](#cite_note-22) The series' first episode screened at the [Biblioteca Vasconcelos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biblioteca_Vasconcelos "Biblioteca Vasconcelos") in [Mexico City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico_City "Mexico City") on 28 November 2024.[[23]](#cite_note-23) Its first two episodes were screened at the [Havana Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Havana_Film_Festival "Havana Film Festival") on 6 December 2024.[[24]](#cite_note-24) The first season, comprising eight episodes, was released in its entirety on Netflix on 11 December 2024.[[25]](#cite_note-25)

A trailer for the second season was released on 17 July 2026.[[26]](#cite_note-26) The second season is scheduled to be released in two parts;[[27]](#cite_note-27) the first seven episodes were released on 5 August 2026 and the series finale will be released on 26 August 2026.[[28]](#cite_note-28)[[29]](#cite_note-29) To promote the second season, Netflix held special screenings in select cities in Colombia.[[1]](#cite_note-De_la_Fuente-2026-1)

## Reception

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=One_Hundred_Years_of_Solitude_(TV_series)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Reception")]

On the [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), 83% of 30 critics' reviews are positive, with an average rating of 7.9/10. The website's consensus reads: "*One Hundred Years of Solitude* faithfully realizes [Gabriel García Márquez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gabriel_García_Márquez "Gabriel García Márquez")'s seminal novel with sumptuous polish, making for an adaptation that is nothing short of magical."[[30]](#cite_note-30) On [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), it has a weighted average score of 80 out of 100, based on 16 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.[[31]](#cite_note-31)

Keith Watson of *[The Telegraph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Telegraph_(London) "The Telegraph (London)")* rated the series five stars out of five, calling it a "faithful but not overly reverent take on Márquez". He commended the cast's performances, specifically those of [Marleyda Soto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marleyda_Soto "Marleyda Soto") and [Claudio Cataño](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudio_Cataño "Claudio Cataño").[[32]](#cite_note-32) Helen Coffey of *[The Independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Independent "The Independent")* called the series "pretty much perfect" and "nothing short of miraculous". She commended the series' creators for staying faithful to the source material while creating "a piece of visually gorgeous storytelling". She also commended the casting, script, cinematography, and music.[[33]](#cite_note-33) Julio Ricardo Varela of [MSNBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MSNBC "MSNBC") wrote that the series provides "countless moments of brilliance that prove creating art from other works of art is still possible." He commended the performances of the entire cast, especially Soto, Cataño, and Marco Antonio González, and noted the care that seemed to have gone into the series' production.[[34]](#cite_note-34) Judy Berman of *[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")* wrote, "Considering the difficulty of the assignment, it's remarkable how close Netflix's splendid *One Hundred Years of Solitude* . . . comes to recreating not just the substance, but also the kinetic spirit of the book." She wrote that the series successfully conveyed the story of the novel without oversimplifying its major themes, including the "ugly but symbolically meaningful aspects of the story, from self-harm to incest". She commended the series' production value, direction, and cinematography.[[35]](#cite_note-35)

Daniel Fienberg of *[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hollywood_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")* called the series a "gorgeous, ambitious adaptation" of the novel that is "honorable and beautiful, if not without flaws." He noted that much of the series' content was taken verbatim from the novel, which "doesn't always work" on screen, and that "everything plays better when the show is at its most figurative and least literal." He commended García López and Mora's direction, calling the series "breathlessly beautiful at times, lyrical and alive and brimming with visual and intellectual ideas." He concluded, "*One Hundred Years of Solitude* may not be as good as *[Underground Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Underground_Railroad_(miniseries) "The Underground Railroad (miniseries)")* or even *[Station Eleven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Station_Eleven_(miniseries) "Station Eleven (miniseries)")*, but it's a worthy and admirable capper for a year of often exceptional prestige adaptations."[[36]](#cite_note-36) Aramide Tinubu of *[Variety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")* called the series "exquisitely detailed and layered in intricate symbolism" and "one of the most faithful page-to-screen adaptations in recent years." She called the performances "exceptional", but said that certain sequences felt dense. Although she found the pacing "too lackadaisical at times", she wrote, "the beauty of *One Hundred Years of Solitude* allows the viewer to absorb every intricately curated frame and moment."[[37]](#cite_note-37) Carly Lane of *[Collider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collider_(website) "Collider (website)")* called the series "a masterpiece in its own right" and wrote, "Not only does the Spanish-language series breathe new life into Márquez's supposedly unfilmable novel, but it also succeeds as a triumph of filmmaking thanks to stunning cinematography and an epic story that spans across multiple generations of the ill-fated Buendía family." She commended the visuals of Paulo Pérez and María Sarasvati, the production design of [Eugenio Caballero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eugenio_Caballero "Eugenio Caballero") and [Bárbara Enríquez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bárbara_Enríquez?action=edit&redlink=1 "Bárbara Enríquez (page does not exist)") [[pt](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bárbara%20Enríquez "pt:Bárbara Enríquez")], and the ensemble's performance.[[38]](#cite_note-38)

Jack Seale of *[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")* rated the series three stars out of five, writing that it "might struggle with the novel's problematic sexual politics, but it's a big, gorgeous adaptation".[[39]](#cite_note-39) Ed Potton of *[The Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Times "The Times")* rated the series two stars out of five, calling it "gorgeous but lethargic" and writing that it "lacks the vibrancy and energy of the novel". He commended the production design of Caballero and Enríquez, but said the series struggled to translate magic realism to the screen.[[40]](#cite_note-40)

args.summary:
One Hundred Years of Solitude (Spanish: Cien años de soledad) is a Colombian television series based on Gabriel García Márquez's 1967 novel of the same name. The series is produced by Netflix, has 16 episodes across 2 seasons, and is filmed entirely in Colombia with a Colombian cast, in Spanish and Wayuu languages. The first season (8 episodes) was released on December 11, 2024. The second season is being released in two parts: the first 7 episodes on August 5, 2026, and the series finale on August 26, 2026.

The series is a drama/magical realism adaptation, directed by Alex García López, Laura Mora, and Carlos Moreno. The cast includes Claudio Cataño as Colonel Aureliano Buendía, Diego Vásquez as José Arcadio Buendía, Marleyda Soto as Úrsula Iguarán, and others. Netflix acquired the rights in 2019; García Márquez had previously refused film adaptations, believing feature films were too short. The production was supported by the author's family, required an open casting call of over 10,000 candidates, and employed nearly 600 crew members. The fictional town of Macondo was built near Alvarado, Tolima, by 1,100 workers in four versions to depict the passage of time.

Critical reception has been positive. On Rotten Tomatoes, 83% of critics' reviews are positive (average 7.9/10), with the consensus calling it a "faithful realization" of the novel. Metacritic gives it a score of 80/100. The series has won several awards, including Best Ibero-American Miniseries or TV series at the 2025 Platino Awards, and multiple Premios India Catalina. The production generated 225 billion COP ($51.8 million USD) for Colombia's economy.

One Hundred Years of Solitude (Cien Años de Soledad) is a drama fantasy television series directed by Alex Garcia Lopez and Laura Mora Ortega, and based on the book by Gabriel García Márquez. Starring Claudio Cataño, Marco González, Jerónimo Barón, Leonardo Soto, Santiago Vasquez, Ella Becerra, and Moreno Borja, the series is the first direct adaptation of Márquez's novel as well as Netflix's most expensive Latin American-made project. It was released on December 11, 2024. One Hundred Years of Solitude was shot in Colombia. Filming locations include Tolima, Cundinamarca, La Guajira and Magdalena.

# Netflix Hit ‘One Hundred Years of Solitude’: Colombia’s Locations From Caribbean Sun to Rose-Tinged Salt Flats, Marshy Mountain Moors, a Mangrove Swamp and That Key Big Tree

By
[John Hopewell](https://variety.com/author/john-hopewell/)

### [John Hopewell](https://variety.com/author/john-hopewell/)

Chief International Correspondent

#### Latest

![Macondo Before Macondo](https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/0-Macondo-Before-Macondo.jpg?w=1000&h=667&crop=1)

Early on in their accaimed TV series adaptation of Gabriel García Márquez’s “[One Hundred Years of Solitude](https://variety.com/t/one-hundred-years-of-solitude/)” [Netflix](https://variety.com/t/netflix/) and Bogota-based producer [Dynamo](https://variety.com/t/dynamo/) (“Narcos”) set out to find Macondo.

First, writers, producers and location managers visited Aracateca, the Nobel Prize winner’s birthplace on Colombia’s Caribbean seaboard. Later they toured Colombia’s Guajira peninsula, its Pacific Coast and Ciénega Grande swamp, capital Bogota’s province and Tolima in the high Andes.

As they had always imagined, they never found Macondo – in the sense of one single village which could easily readapted into the icon magical realism. The idea, however, from the very beginning was to build Macondo from scratch.

### Popular on Variety

### Popular on Variety

Those fam trips, however, left multiple health hostages to fortune.

Most of the action of “One Hundred Years of Solitude” – the novel and series – in reality takes place in a relatively small strip of territory in Colombia’s far Caribbean north.

Directed by Alex García and Laura Mora, the series’ story begins in a ranchería –  a traditional village somewhere on the plains outside Riohacha on Colombia’s Caribbean coast. It then crosses the soaring Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta and remains for most of the rest of Season 1 in Macondo north-west of the Sierra, in the Ciénaga Grande, but so near to the Caribbean Sea that the later discovery of its proximity breaks Macondo founder José Arcadio Buendía’s spirit.

In contrast, the series’ locations range from Guajira in the north to Alvarado, Tolima, in central Colombia’s Andes. Reasons for that range explain very much the locations of “One Hundred Years of Solitude. 10 takes and photos:

### **Looking for Macondo**

Macondo couldn’t be any old place, however. Locations are very much a matter of logistics. “The biggest challenge was to find locations that were visually incredible but also practicable,” says Macondo location manager, Cristiano D. Toro. “One request I made was that Macondo had to be near an airport. But most importantly, we’re a very large production. If I have problems with crew, cameras, for example, we needed to be able to move easily, and given our long shooting days, it’s always best to have Bogotá near,” recalls Carolina Caicedo, executive producer of of “One Hundred Years of Solitude.”

![](https://variety.com/wp-content/themes/pmc-variety-2020/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif)

### **Macondo Ground Zero: A Wild Tree Hunt**

Macondo also wouldn’t be built quite from scratch. In a drive for authenticity, art director Eugenio Caballero requested any Macondo to have high mountains behind and be built around a real-life big tree which would end up at the center of Macondo’s square. And it couldn’t be any tree either. It needed to allow enough space between it and key buildings such the school and church, and catch sunrise light one side and evening sun on the other, remembers Emerson Espinosa, also “One Hundred Years of Solitude” location manager. A large caucho cartagénero was found on the Arizona ranch, vast green pastures outside Alvarado, less than an hour’s drive from Tolima capital Ibagúe, itself an hour’s flight to Bogóta. Colombia’s real life steep-backed Western Andes rise behind Alvarado. Topping them in the series are the snow capped peaks of Sierra Nevada de la Marta, added by VFX. Macondo – its backlot site for the two biggest sets at least, including the biggest,capturing Macondo in its largest splendor from EP. 4 to Ep. 6 in Season 1 – had been found.

![](https://variety.com/wp-content/themes/pmc-variety-2020/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif)

### **Creating Locations**

Which aren’t explicitly in the novel.

One example: “On Sunday, effectively, Rebeca arrived. She had made a difficult journey from Manaure,” Garcia Márquez writes in “One Hundred Years of Solitude,” chapter three. He makes no explicit mention, however, of the feature for which Manaure, on Colombia’s northernmost La Guajira coast, is best known: Its extraordinary salt flats.

When Netflix optioned the novel’s adaptation rights in 2019, García Marquez’s widow, Mercedes Barcha, has widow and sons Rodrigo García (the distinguished director, “Albert Nobbs”) and Gonzalo García Barcha insisted that the series was shot in Colombia by Colombians. Rodrígo García also gave directors Alex García and Laura Mora total creative freedom.

![](https://variety.com/wp-content/themes/pmc-variety-2020/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif)

Naturally enough, in a supremely visual (and more narrative-driven) medium such as TV, they often take it. “Somebody’s coming,” an adolescent José Aureliano predicts at the end of Ep. 2. Its climax is dramatic but also aesthetic: a shot of the extraordinary real-life rose-tinted salt plains of Manaure. Cut to Ep. 3’s opening as a cart and donkey are driven across the same salt plains, this time chalk white and as hard as ice, carrying Rebeca. Netflix popularised the idea that series have to grab the attention in its first few minutes. Here, the series has done so in a one-minute sequence thanks to an extraordinary location.

![](https://variety.com/wp-content/themes/pmc-variety-2020/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif)

### **One Hundred Year’s Industrial Agenda**

There’s also an industrial agenda at work. Colombia is already South America’s biggest big international shoot hub, with 64 projects approved over 2023-24 amounting to a total $249.8 million in investment in the country. The best way to encourage more shoots to come is by proclaiming Colombia’s production capacity in a banner series which captures global attention. Enter “One Hundred Years of Solitude.” Over two-parts and 16 hours, the series forefronts one of the main reasons why international shoots set up in any country: the stunning variety of locations. “The objective of the series in part is to show Colombia in all its diversity,” says Espinosa.

![](https://variety.com/wp-content/themes/pmc-variety-2020/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif)

**Finding Macondo All Over Colombia**

So it’s no coincidence that the series finds Macondo all over Colombia, in a total 32 provinces (departamentos), whether a street-corner building backed by modern high-rises (above), or a perfectly preserved dining room in a private house (below) or the facade of an 1890’s pharmacy. The first’s dining room (below) was used to shoot scenes in Arcadio’s house. It’s not so dissimilar to Ursula’s dining room either (below). Director Alex García shot interiors in the pharmacy while its facade helped inspire that of anarchist Alirio Noguera’s shop in Ep. 2.

![](https://variety.com/wp-content/themes/pmc-variety-2020/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif)
![](https://variety.com/wp-content/themes/pmc-variety-2020/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif)

### **The Dazzling Light of the Caribbean**

And “A Hundred Years of Solitude” proclaims the diversity of Colombian locations. The biggest location outside Macondo in terms of series time spent there, is cousins José Arcadio and Úrsula’s native village where they wed in Ep. 1., which begins the series broad narrative. Created adapting or building for scratch huts in an old ranchería near Valledupar, the main town east of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, the opening scenes captures the climate of the Caribbean seaboard. Throwing open the shutters of a window (Ep. 1, minute 7.48), Úrsula reveals the dazzling light, blue skies and low-lying trade wind cumulus clouds of the Caribbean seaboard (above) plus other huts simulating the mud, cactus trunk wood and palm roofs of a Guajira Wayuu ranchería, notes Toro.

![](https://variety.com/wp-content/themes/pmc-variety-2020/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif)

### **”Smooth White Rocks Like Prehistoric Eggs”**

It’s one of García Marquez’s most famous descriptions in the novel “One Hundred Years of Solitude,” ending its second sentence, to describe the bed of the Río Ancho beside on whose banks Macondo was founded. Río Ancho was shot in a river descending from the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta to the Caribbean Sea near to Dibulla in western La Guajira. Macondo 0-1, as it is called, the rudimentary village of Macondo, was built at Garanchal Ranch, Venadillo, a 20-minute drive north go Alvardo, on the edge of the Magdalena River, Colombia’s longest, in Tolima. But it doesn’t have rocks like dinosaur’s eggs. So Río Ancho scenes, including José Arcadio¡s dream, were shot 700 miles northwards. Locations is the art of the possible.

![](https://variety.com/wp-content/themes/pmc-variety-2020/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif)

### **The Series Highpoint**

Though tropical, Colombian capital Bogotá is lodged in high mountains, seeming like Scotland when it rains or hails, a mist enveloping its northern parts. Nowhere is colder and more inhospitable in the whole of Season 1 than Episode’s 1 high mountain moors scenes where José Arcadio’s expedition edges along a path half way up a precipice, a mule slipping into the void. As rain later lashes their tent, José Arcadia assures the shivering rest of the expedition that they’re very near to getting to the sea. These scenes were shot in the Páramo de Chingaza, a national natural park two hours car ride east of Bogotá, whose peaks rise to 13,000 feet. But ease of access remains key. So it’s no coincidence that one of its wildest locations also has a road snaking between its peaks (below). The road, naturally, was not seen in the series.

![](https://variety.com/wp-content/themes/pmc-variety-2020/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif)

### **Securing Locations**

One key to a location is finding it. Another is preparing it. Natural locations can also change, varying according to season, Espinosa observes. Near to the Rio Ancho and Palomino, on the Magdalena/La Guajira border, the location team found a swamp which was a mix of mangroves, river and salt water. “It was marvellous, with beautiful, brilliant water which gave off reflections, reaching up to people’s chest,” Espinosa remembers.

![](https://variety.com/wp-content/themes/pmc-variety-2020/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif)

The locations team was worried, however, that the swamp was too slippery for actors, crew and animals, its bed made up of mud and roots. The second time they visited, however, water levels were far lower. “So we cleaned the swamp bed, so that footing was safe when it had more water,” he adds. Scenes of José Arcadio and friends sloshing through the swamp, completely lost, are among the most memorable of Season 1.

![](https://variety.com/wp-content/themes/pmc-variety-2020/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif)

### **One of the Series’ Most Spectacular Locations is Heard But Hardly Seen**

During the expedition, Úrsula gives birth to José Arcadio, terrified the baby will have a pig’s tail. Dynamo chose a special site: Tolima’s Cuevas del Mohan,  – a huge 160-foot waterfall cascading down to a small cave beside a river. “The access was not easy; however, everything necessary was done to make it easy and suitable for the crew and for the baby, who was our priority on that shooting day to ensure their safety. It was necessary to adjust the roads for the access of all the trucks and all the logistics involved in this night shoot,” Toro recalls. The birth scene is shot at night. The walls of the cave can only be seen briefly behind, but the waterfall can be heard. The sense of water is always present, he adds.

![](https://variety.com/wp-content/themes/pmc-variety-2020/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif)

args.summary:
This Variety article (by John Hopewell) details the extensive location scouting and production design for Netflix's acclaimed adaptation of Gabriel García Márquez's "One Hundred Years of Solitude," produced by Bogotá-based Dynamo ("Narcos"). The series, directed by Alex García and Laura Mora, was filmed across 32 provinces (departamentos) in Colombia, with the fictional town of Macondo built from scratch rather than found as a single existing location.

Key locations include:
- **Alvarado, Tolima**: The primary Macondo backlot was built on the Arizona ranch, centered around a large caucho cartagénero tree. The real-life Western Andes rise behind, with snow-capped Sierra Nevada peaks added via VFX.
- **Manaure, La Guajira**: The rose-tinted salt flats were used for Rebeca's dramatic arrival (Ep. 2-3), capturing the series' visual aesthetic.
- **Valledupar area**: An old ranchería near the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta was used for José Arcadio and Úrsula's native village (Ep. 1), capturing the Caribbean seaboard's light and climate.
- **Río Ancho, near Dibulla**: The river with "smooth white rocks like prehistoric eggs" (from the novel's famous description) was shot 700 miles north of the main Macondo set.
- **Páramo de Chingaza**: The high mountain moors (13,000 ft peaks) used for the expedition scenes in Ep. 1, where José Arcadio's mule slips into the void.
- **Ciénaga Grande swamp**: A mangrove/river/saltwater mix that was cleaned and prepared for the memorable swamp-crossing scenes.
- **Cuevas del Mohan, Tolima**: A 160-foot waterfall cave used for the night birth scene of José Arcadio.

The article notes that García Márquez's widow Mercedes Barcha and sons insisted the series be shot in Colombia by Colombians. Carolina Caicedo (executive producer) emphasized the need for locations near airports and Bogotá for logistical reasons. The series also serves an industrial agenda to showcase Colombia's production capacity, as the country approved 64 international projects over 2023-24 totaling $249.8 million in investment.

# One Hundred Years of Solitude – Film Locations in Colombia

[Colombia](https://www.selectlatinamerica.co.uk/category/colombia/), [General](https://www.selectlatinamerica.co.uk/category/general/) /  3 January 2025

The Netflix series *One Hundred Years of Solitude*, based on Gabriel García Márquez’s iconic novel, was primarily filmed in [**Colombia**](https://www.selectlatinamerica.co.uk/colombia/). The production sought to capture the essence of the fictional town of Macondo, the main setting of the novel, and the rich landscape that influenced Márquez’s writing.

One Hundred Years of Solitude is a new TV series based on Gabriel García Márquez’s famous book. This novel is one of the most important works of the 20th century. It has taken years to see it come to life on screen. The story is about the Buendía family and their lives in the magical town of Macondo. It follows them through love, loss, and fate over seven generations. The series explores themes like loneliness, family, and the passage of time. The show captures the magical realism that made the novel so beloved.

Adapted from the 1967 novel written by Gabriel García Márquez, ‘One Hundred Years of Solitude’ follows José Arcadio Buendía and Úrsula Iguarán. The cousins marry against the will of their parents and leave their village to start afresh. On the journey, the couple meet friends and adventurers before arriving at Macondo, which has an ominous historical significance, leading them to a century of solitude.

One Hundred Years of Solitude’ is filmed in Colombia, particularly in Tolima, La Guajira, Magdalena, Cesar, and Cundinamarca.

### **Tolima**

To bring the fictional town of Macondo to life, the film team set up near Alvarado and Ibagué in the Tolima department of Colombia and built the town from the ground up, with birds nesting in the trees and dogs roaming the streets.

#### **The Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta**:

This mountainous region was used to capture the natural beauty of the landscapes around Macondo. The mountains, lush forests, and rural settings provide a backdrop to the story.The region is magical for birdwatchers. They rise early and follow local naturalist guides for the chance to observe some of the 628 bird species. Other attractions include treks to spectacular waterfalls and nearby ruins.

#### **La Guajira Peninsula**:

This area, with its unique desert and coastal landscapes, offered a distinct atmosphere that reflects the isolation and mysticism found in the novel. There is little infrastructure and few places to stay. There are basic cabins for hardy travellers. Colombia’s largest indigenous group are found here, the Wayuu. It is an ideal place for experiential tourism: driving over dunes, boat trips and fishing with the local community.

#### **Ciénaga**:

A town on Colombia’s Caribbean coast, known for its history and proximity to wetlands, this location was another key filming spot.

#### **Vélez, Santander**:

A town in the central part of the country, known for its preserved colonial architecture and scenic surroundings, also served as part of Macondo.

The production aimed to use Colombia’s diverse environments to bring the novel’s vivid, dream-like world to life while respecting its Colombian cultural roots. The series, being a faithful adaptation, features these locations as part of its effort to capture the essence of the novel’s setting.

### **The Macondo Route** **tourist locations**

This marks a perfect opportunity to introduce two new tourist routes focused on the life and work of Gabriel García Márquez. Starting in 2025, Select Latin America will offer a 10-day Macondo Route tour, beginning in Bogotá and passing through Zipaquirá, Aracataca, Mompox, Barranquilla, and Cartagena. A second, shorter route will start in Santa Marta, pass through Aracataca and Mompox, and end in Cartagena. On this journey discover the Colombia that shaped his stories: a land of arid deserts, tropical jungles, misty mountains, and colonial towns suspended in time. Step into the living history of his imaginary universe and feel the blur between the past and the present, the mythical and the real.

We can also offer a two-day trip out of Bogotá to visit the film’s main setting in Alvarado, a small town in Tolima Department. This charming village still preserves its colonial ambience. Take lunch here, before visiting the *Iglesia San Antonio de Padua* and exploring the village. In the afternoon, continue to Ibagué, to spend the night.

#### **Cartagena:**

The Clock Gate, mentioned in “Living to Tell the Tale,” where García Márquez first experienced the city he loved deeply.

Cartagena is the jewel of Colombia’s Caribbean coast. This sun-drenched walled city was once home to Gabriel García Márquez — or ‘Gabo’, as he is affectionately known to Colombians. The port is full of life and from here one can take boat trips to tropical islands. Some of the colonial mansions have been turned into [boutque hotels](https://www.selectlatinamerica.co.uk/colombia/colombia-hotels/cartagena-hotels).

#### **Barranquilla:**

El Prado Hotel, the setting of his first formal dance with Doña Mercedes, and the Socorro Church where they were married.

#### **Aracataca:**

Aracataca is the birthplace of Gabo, a quiet, sweltering town 230km north in the Sierra Nevada. A place of tropical forests and banana plantations is where Gabriel García Márquez’s grew up. His former childhood home is now open to the public, the Casa Museo.

#### **Bogotá:**

San Francisco Church, where Gabo accidentally met his uncle, Colonel Valdiblánquez, at the atrium.

Bogotá is Colombia’s capital. Gabo worked as a journalist here in the 1940’s. The historic centre has not changed much, with colonial buildings and coffee bars around the Plaza Bolívar. Today there is a thriving food and art scene.

#### Mompox

Mompox is a small, sleepy colonial town in the swamps of Bolivar province, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Gabo spent much time here, and it resembles Macondo, the setting of One Hundred Years of Solitude. A fascinating place but is very hot and sticky. By road, it’s a six-hour drive from Cartagena, or a short helicopter ride. Stay at the excellent Casa San Rafael, a restored 17th-century colonial house. It can also be reached along the Magdalena River, there is a 4-day river cruise from Cartagena which stop here. You can take canoe rides into the wetlands where bird life and monkeys abound.

#### **Zipaquirá:**

The house of Fernanda del Carpio, now the Zipaquirá Museum, which features an inventory of items mentioned in *One Hundred Years of Solitude.*

# Cien años de soledad: los increíbles paisajes donde Netflix filmó la segunda temporada

El rodaje de la segunda temporada de Cien años de soledad se llevó a cabo en escenarios naturales de diversas regiones de Colombia.

* ## [Netflix: la miniserie japonesa donde cada plato esconde una historia de amor, soledad y segundas oportunidades](https://www.quever.news/netflix/netflix-la-miniserie-japonesa-donde-cada-plato-esconde-una-historia-amor-soledad-y-segundas-oportunidades-n1575088 "Que Ver | Netflix: la miniserie japonesa donde cada plato esconde una historia de amor, soledad y segundas oportunidades")

Cien años de soledad se filmó en distintos lugares de Colombia

Netflix

El regreso de Macondo a la pantalla despertó una pregunta inevitable entre los fanáticos de la obra de Gabriel García Márquez: dónde queda el pueblo que se ve en la **serie** de **[Netflix](https://www.quever.news/temas/netflix-7.html)**. La respuesta está enteramente en Colombia, ya que la segunda parte de  ***[Cien años de soledad](https://www.quever.news/temas/cien-anos-de-soledad-12812.html/1)*** se rodó de punta a punta en territorio colombiano, con un imponente set central en el departamento de Tolima y locaciones repartidas en La Guajira, Magdalena, Cesar y Cundinamarca.

El corazón de la producción de **Netflix** late cerca de Alvarado, en Tolima, donde se levantó un decorado monumental concebido como un organismo vivo. Ese escenario no permaneció estático: fue transformándose a medida que avanzaba el relato para reflejar cada etapa de Macondo, desde su crecimiento inicial y la llegada del ferrocarril hasta la modernización del pueblo y su inevitable decadencia final.

## Tráiler de la segunda parte de Cien años de Soledad

Cien años de soledad: Segunda parte | Tráiler oficial | Netflix

Pero la magia visual de la **serie** no se explica solo por ese gigantesco set. El departamento de Magdalena aportó los paisajes ribereños y esa atmósfera caribeña tan ligada a Aracataca, la localidad natal del premio Nobel colombiano que inspiró el universo de la novela. Allí la producción encontró la luz y los tonos que remiten directamente al imaginario original del escritor.

## Desiertos, sierras y montañas: los otros escenarios del rodaje de la serie de Netflix

La geografía colombiana desplegó toda su diversidad al servicio de **Cien años de soledad**. En La Guajira se registraron las zonas áridas y desérticas, con guiños visuales a las dunas del norte del país, mientras que el departamento de Cesar sumó entornos de vegetación exuberante en las estribaciones de la Sierra de Perijá, un contraste que enriquece la paleta visual de la historia.

args.key_excerpts: The second part of Cien años de soledad was shot from end to end in Colombian territory, with an imposing central set in the department of Tolima and locations spread across La Guajira, Magdalena, Cesar and Cundinamarca., The heart of the Netflix production beats near Alvarado, in Tolima, where a monumental set was built conceived as a living organism., In La Guajira, the arid and desert zones were recorded, while the department of Cesar added lush vegetation environments in the foothills of the Sierra de Perijá., The journey is completed in Cundinamarca, where the Netflix teams took advantage of the mountainous areas, forests and bodies of water near the Bogotá savanna to build the textures of magical realism that run through the entire adaptation.
args.summary: The article reports that the second season of Netflix's "Cien años de soledad" (One Hundred Years of Solitude) was filmed entirely in Colombia, with the main set located in the Tolima department near Alvarado, where a monumental, evolving set was built to represent Macondo at different stages of its history. Additional filming locations include La Guajira for arid and desert landscapes, Magdalena for riverine and Caribbean atmospheres reminiscent of Gabriel García Márquez's hometown Aracataca, Cesar for lush vegetation in the Sierra de Perijá foothills, and Cundinamarca for mountainous areas, forests, and water bodies near the Bogotá savanna. The second part of the series is now available on Netflix.

***Cien años de soledad*** es una serie de televisión [colombiana](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia "Colombia") basada en la novela [homónima](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cien_años_de_soledad "Cien años de soledad") escrita por el colombiano [Gabriel García Márquez](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gabriel_García_Márquez "Gabriel García Márquez") en 1967. Dirigida por Alex García López y [Laura Mora](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Mora "Laura Mora"), la serie es producida por [Dynamo](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dynamo_(productora) "Dynamo (productora)") y distribuida por [Netflix](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix"). Está protagonizada por [Claudio Cataño](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudio_Cataño "Claudio Cataño"), Marco González, Leonardo Soto, Susana Morales, Ella Becerra, Carlos Suárez, Moreno Borja y [Viña Machado](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viña_Machado "Viña Machado"), entre otros actores que se irán sumando a lo largo de la serie.[[1]](#cite_note-1)*Cien años de soledad* se estrenó el 11 de diciembre de 2024.[[2]](#cite_note-2)[[3]](#cite_note-3)[[4]](#cite_note-:0-4)

## Sinopsis

[[editar](/w/index.php?title=Cien_a%C3%B1os_de_soledad_(serie_de_televisi%C3%B3n)&action=edit&section=1 "Editar sección: Sinopsis")]

Al casarse en contra de la voluntad de sus padres, los primos [José Arcadio Buendía](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/José_Arcadio_Buendía "José Arcadio Buendía") (Marco Antonio González Ospina) y [Úrsula Iguarán](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Úrsula_Iguarán "Úrsula Iguarán") (Susana Morales Cañas) dejan atrás su pueblo y emprenden un largo viaje en busca de un nuevo hogar. Acompañados por amigos y aventureros, su periplo culmina con la fundación de un utópico pueblo a las orillas de un río de piedras prehistóricas que bautizan [Macondo](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macondo "Macondo"). Varias generaciones de la estirpe de los Buendía marcarán el devenir de este pueblo mítico, atormentadas por la locura, los amores imposibles, una guerra sangrienta y absurda, y el miedo a una terrible maldición que las condena, sin esperanza alguna, a cien años de soledad.[[4]](#cite_note-:0-4)

## Producción

[[editar](/w/index.php?title=Cien_a%C3%B1os_de_soledad_(serie_de_televisi%C3%B3n)&action=edit&section=8 "Editar sección: Producción")]

[Netflix](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") adquirió los derechos de *[Cien años de soledad](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cien_años_de_soledad "Cien años de soledad")* en 2019.[[5]](#cite_note-5) Antes de su fallecimiento en 2014, el autor Gabriel García Márquez había rechazado la venta de los derechos de la novela, argumentando que no creía que las limitaciones de tiempo de una película fueran suficientes para una adaptación.[[6]](#cite_note-6) La serie se filmó con el apoyo de la familia de García Márquez, quien solicitó que la producción se realizara en Colombia, con actores colombianos y en castellano.[[7]](#cite_note-dup-0-94-7)

Basada en la obra maestra de Márquez, bajo la dirección de Laura Mora y Alex García López, *Cien años de soledad* representa uno de los proyectos audiovisuales más ambiciosos de la historia de Latinoamérica.

La serie fue filmada íntegramente en Colombia, específicamente en [La Guajira](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Guajira "La Guajira"), [Magdalena](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magdalena_(Colombia) "Magdalena (Colombia)"), [Cesar](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cesar "Cesar"), [Cundinamarca](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cundinamarca "Cundinamarca") y [Tolima](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tolima "Tolima").[[8]](#cite_note-8) El rodaje tuvo lugar de mayo a diciembre de 2023.[[9]](#cite_note-9) El pueblo ficticio de [Macondo](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macondo "Macondo") fue construido cerca de [Ibagué](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibagué "Ibagué").[[10]](#cite_note-10)[[7]](#cite_note-dup-0-94-7)[[11]](#cite_note-11) Se construyeron cuatro versiones del pueblo para mostrar el paso del tiempo a medida que avanza la serie. [[12]](#cite_note-12)

 
> Como cineasta, como colombiana, ha sido un honor y un enorme reto trabajar en un proyecto de la complejidad y responsabilidad de *Cien años de soledad*, tratando siempre de entender la diferencia entre el lenguaje literario y el audiovisual, para poder construir imágenes que contengan algo de la belleza, la poesía y la profundidad de una obra que ha impactado al mundo entero. Lo hemos hecho con amor y respeto por la novela, con la ayuda de un equipo técnico y humano excepcional.

### Audición

[[editar](/w/index.php?title=Cien_a%C3%B1os_de_soledad_(serie_de_televisi%C3%B3n)&action=edit&section=9 "Editar sección: Audición")]

El reparto fue elegido a través de una audición abierta a mediados de 2022.[[13]](#cite_note-13) El equipo de *casting* vio más de 10.000 candidatos para los 25 papeles principales. [[14]](#cite_note-«Clarke-2024»-14) Sólo el 30% del reparto está compuesto por actores profesionales.[[15]](#cite_note-15) Además del reparto principal, también se seleccionaron 20.000 extras para el rodaje.[[16]](#cite_note-16) El reparto se filtró parcialmente el 26 de abril de 2023.[[17]](#cite_note-17)

### Filmación

[[editar](/w/index.php?title=Cien_a%C3%B1os_de_soledad_(serie_de_televisi%C3%B3n)&action=edit&section=10 "Editar sección: Filmación")]

La fotografía principal tuvo lugar de mayo a diciembre de 2023.[[18]](#cite_note-«Kay-2024»-18) La serie se rodó íntegramente en Colombia,[[19]](#cite_note-19)[[20]](#cite_note-20) específicamente en [La Guajira](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Departamento_de_La_Guajira "Departamento de La Guajira"), [Magdalena](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Departamento_del_Magdalena "Departamento del Magdalena"), [Cesar](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Departamento_del_Cesar "Departamento del Cesar"), [Cundinamarca](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Departamento_de_Cundinamarca "Departamento de Cundinamarca") y [Tolima](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Departamento_del_Tolima "Departamento del Tolima"). [[21]](#cite_note-21) El pueblo ficticio de [Macondo](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macondo "Macondo") fue construido cerca de [Alvarado](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alvarado_(Tolima) "Alvarado (Tolima)"), Tolima, y requirió la mano de obra de 1.100 trabajadores. Se construyeron cuatro versiones del pueblo para mostrar el paso del tiempo a medida que avanza la serie. Los productores compraron muebles en tiendas de antigüedades locales y encargaron a artesanos locales la confección de telas y objetos para los decorados.[[14]](#cite_note-«Clarke-2024»-14) El rodaje requirió un equipo de casi 600 personas, todas ellas de Colombia.[[22]](#cite_note-22)

Netflix informó que la producción de la serie generó 225 mil millones de [COP](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peso_colombiano "Peso colombiano") (51,8 millones de [dólares](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dólar_estadounidense "Dólar estadounidense")) para la economía de Colombia.[[23]](#cite_note-23) La producción de la segunda parte de la serie comenzó en febrero de 2025.[[24]](#cite_note-24)

## Recepción crítica

[[editar](/w/index.php?title=Cien_a%C3%B1os_de_soledad_(serie_de_televisi%C3%B3n)&action=edit&section=12 "Editar sección: Recepción crítica")]

En el sitio web agregador de críticas [Rotten Tomatoes](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), el 94% de las 16 reseñas de los críticos son positivas, con una puntuación media de 8,6/10.[[32]](#cite_note-32) En el sitio web [Metacritic](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic") tiene una puntuación media ponderada de 79 sobre 100, basada en 10 críticas, lo que indica críticas «generalmente favorables».[[33]](#cite_note-33)

Keith Watson, de *[The Telegraph](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Telegraph "The Telegraph")*, calificó la serie con cinco estrellas sobre cinco, escribiendo: «Lo que se obtiene con esta fiel pero no excesivamente reverente toma de Márquez es una historia humana cosida sobre un tejido que cubre temas eternos». Elogió las interpretaciones del reparto como «ejemplares», en concreto las de Marleyda Soto y Claudio Cataño.[[34]](#cite_note-34) Helen Coffey, de *[The Independent](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Independent "The Independent")*, calificó la serie de «prácticamente perfecta», escribiendo: «Parece poco menos que milagrosa. Al igual que el hecho de que los creadores hayan logrado lo que parecía imposible: mantenerse fieles al material original y, al mismo tiempo, traducirlo con arte en una pieza de narración visualmente magnífica». Elogió el reparto, el guion, la fotografía y la música.[[35]](#cite_note-35) Julio Ricardo Varela, de [MSNBC](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/MSNBC "MSNBC"), escribió que la serie ofrece «innumerables momentos de brillantez que demuestran que crear arte a partir de otras obras de arte sigue siendo posible». Elogió las actuaciones de todo el reparto, en concreto las de Soto, Cataño y Marco Antonio González, y destacó el cuidado que parecía haberse puesto en la producción de la serie.[[36]](#cite_note-36)

Daniel Fienberg, de *[The Hollywood Reporter](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hollywood_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")*, calificó la serie de «magnífica y ambiciosa adaptación» de la novela, «honorable y hermosa, aunque no exenta de defectos». Señaló que gran parte del contenido de la serie se tomó textualmente de la novela, lo que «no siempre funciona» cuando se representa en pantalla y que «todo funciona mejor cuando la serie es más figurativa y menos literal». Elogió la dirección de García López y Mora, calificando la serie de «de una belleza sin aliento a veces, lírica y viva y rebosante de ideas visuales e intelectuales». En última instancia, concluyó que «Cien años de soledad» puede que no sea tan buena como *[El ferrocarril subterráneo](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_ferrocarril_subterráneo "El ferrocarril subterráneo")* o incluso *[Estación Once](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estación_Once "Estación Once")*, pero es un digno y admirable broche de oro para un año de adaptaciones de prestigio a menudo excepcionales»."[[37]](#cite_note-37) Aramide Tinubu de *[Variety](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Variety_(magazine) "Variety (magazine)")* calificó la serie de «exquisitamente detallada y llena de intrincados simbolismos» y de «una de las adaptaciones de la página a la pantalla más fieles de los últimos años». Elogió las interpretaciones del reparto, que calificó de «excepcionales», pero señaló que algunas secuencias le parecían densas. Aunque cree que el ritmo de la serie es «demasiado lento a veces», señala que «la belleza de “Cien años de soledad” permite al espectador absorber cada fotograma y cada momento». [[38]](#cite_note-38) Carly Lane de *[Collider](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collider_(website) "Collider (website)")* calificó la serie de «obra maestra por derecho propio» y escribió: «La serie en español no sólo insufla nueva vida a la novela supuestamente imposible de filmar de Márquez, sino que también triunfa como realización cinematográfica gracias a una impresionante fotografía y a una historia épica que abarca varias generaciones de la «malograda familia Buendía». Elogió los efectos visuales de Paulo Pérez y María Sarasvati, el diseño de producción de [Eugenio Caballero](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eugenio_Caballero "Eugenio Caballero") y Bárbara Enríquez, y la interpretación del conjunto.[[39]](#cite_note-39)

Jack Seale de *[The Guardian](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Guardian "The Guardian")* calificó la serie con tres estrellas sobre cinco, escribiendo que «puede que tenga problemas con la problemática política sexual de la novela, pero es una gran y magnífica adaptación.[[40]](#cite_note-40) Ed Potton de *[The Times](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Times "The Times")* calificó la serie con dos estrellas sobre cinco, calificándola de «magnífica pero letárgica» y escribiendo que «carece de la vitalidad y energía de la novela». Elogió el diseño de producción de Caballero y Enríquez, pero señaló que la serie tenía dificultades para trasladar el realismo mágico a la pantalla.[[41]](#cite_note-41)

args.summary:
"Cien años de soledad" is a Colombian television series based on Gabriel García Márquez's 1967 novel of the same name. Directed by Alex García López and Laura Mora, produced by Dynamo and distributed by Netflix, the series stars Claudio Cataño, Marco González, Susana Morales, and others. The series premiered on December 11, 2024, with an 8-episode first season; a second season is planned.

**Synopsis:** The story follows cousins José Arcadio Buendía and Úrsula Iguarán who, after marrying against their parents' wishes, leave their village and found the utopian town of Macondo. The series traces multiple generations of the Buendía family, haunted by madness, impossible loves, a bloody war, and a curse of one hundred years of solitude.

**Production:** Netflix acquired rights in 2019. García Márquez had previously refused to sell film rights, believing film couldn't capture the novel. Filmed entirely in Colombia (La Guajira, Magdalena, Cesar, Cundinamarca, Tolima) from May to December 2023, with Macondo constructed near Ibagué. Four versions of the town were built to show the passage of time. Over 10,000 candidates auditioned for 25 main roles; only 30% of the cast are professional actors. The production employed nearly 600 crew members, all Colombian, and generated 225 billion COP ($51.8 million) for Colombia's economy.

**Critical Reception:** The series received strong reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes, 94% of 16 critic reviews are positive (average 8.6/10). Metacritic score is 79/100, indicating "generally favorable" reviews. Critics praised the faithful adaptation, performances (especially Marleyda Soto and Claudio Cataño), cinematography, and production design, though some noted pacing issues and challenges translating magical realism to screen.

# Los bellos destinos en Colombia donde se filmó la serie de ‘Cien años de soledad’

Recientemente, Netflix nos mostró un avance de la serie que lleva el mismo nombre de la aclamada novela de Gabriel García Márquez, y además de gozar de la historia y de actuaciones imperdibles; estamos listos para disfrutar de los paisajes y destinos que veremos en la serie, y que por fortuna, ¡existen en Colombia!

Por [Diana Garrido](/autor/diana/197)

Está por estrenarse ‘Cien años de soledad’, y estos son los lugares en donde se filmó.Cortesía Netflix

Este año **tendremos la serie *Cien años de soledad* en Netflix**. La historia es retrata fielmente la novela del mismo nombre, obra de Gabriel García Márquez, quien la escribió en tan solo 18 meses: de 1965 a 1966 cuando vivía en la Ciudad de México. En ese tiempo, él solo tuvo dinero para mandar la primera mitad a una editorial en Argentina, pero no se dio cuenta de que envió la segunda parte, así que los editores se emocionaron tanto con la historia que ellos financiaron el envío de la primera sección. Así, en 1967 se publicó la primera edición en Buenos Aires y desde entonces, la novela es considerada una obra maestra contemporánea.

Así, el 17 de abril, Netflix **reveló el primer corte de *Cien años de soledad*,** y además de darnos una idea de lo que se retratará, pudimos ver algunas de las locaciones en las que desarrolla la historia de la familia Buendía en el pueblo ficticio Macondo. Bajo la dirección de Laura Mora y Alex García López, presenta los espacios creados para la producción que, en realidad, sí existen en Colombia, lugar que fungió como sede principal del rodaje. Así que antes de que se estrene en la plataforma, ¿por qué no visitarlos y gozar de los paisajes tan bellos del país”.

La Guajira.Juan Pablo Jou-Valencia / Unsplash

## La Guajira

Guajira pertenece a su vez, a uno de los 32 departamentos en los que se divide Colombia. Está situado al norte del país y **limita con el mar Caribe y con Venezuela**. Está constituido por 15 municipios y desde la década de los 70, ha sido hogar de inmigrantes de países del Medio Oriente, por lo que la demografía ha crecido considerablemente. En esta zona se encuentran tres parques naturales y cinco pueblos nativo-americanos. Asimismo, **se le conoce por ser cuna del vallenato**, por lo que recibe una gran cantidad de turistas al año.

Magdalena.Berend Leupen / Unsplash

## Magdalena

El nombre proviene del río que predomina en el lugar. Está conformado por cuatro cuencas hidrográficas que abastece a varias zonas del país, por lo que los cuerpos de agua son fascinantes y que a su vez, están rodeados de naturaleza netamente verde que proporciona oxígeno y, además, zonas perfectas para hacer *hiking* y más. Cabe señalar que **Magdalena es el lugar de nacimiento de [Gabriel García Márquez](https://www.admagazine.com/articulos/libros-de-gabriel-garcia-marquez-que-deberias-leer),** aunque sus últimos días de vida los pasó en la Ciudad de México.

#### Instagram content

## Cesar

Los paisajes, la naturaleza y la cultura se combinan en Cesar, especialmente, en la capital Valledupar. **El poeta Fernando Dangond inspiró gran parte de su obra en este,** que dicho sea de paso, es su lugar de nacimiento. El lugar se destaca por sus paisajes naturales en los que se pueden realizar actividades como *camping,* caminatas y ecoturismo en general. Uno de los espacios más conocidos y concurridos es El Mojao, que es un lugar con aguas cristalinas, cascadas y pozos en los que las personas utilizan como balneario, ya que además hay áreas de descanso y convivencia.

Cudinamarca.De ca / Unsplash

## Cundinamarca

Esta región [está muy cerca de Bogotá](https://www.admagazine.com/articulos/bogota-colombia-ad-city-guides-con-kelly-talamas) y se trata de un lugar natural que posee la laguna de Guatavita, una de las más importantes en Colombia. Aunque no hay una ruta de transporte público directo, es muy sencillo llegar. Es un sitio histórico muy tranquilo que sirve como escaparate del bullicio de la ciudad para descansar y retomar el aliento, así como para **probar las delicias culinarias típicas de la región y de Colombia en sí**. Es un sitio que conserva edificaciones antiguas y siguen siendo utilizadas como parte de la comunidad.

Tolima.JULY ROLDAN / Unsplash

## Tolima

Este departamento tiene en su haber a **Falan, una “ciudad perdida”.** Esta es, en realidad, una serie de ruinas que datan del siglo XVII debido a la invasión española. Así, se ha convertido en una de las zonas más atractivas del lugar ya que, además, está rodeada de la selva, de murallas naturales y bodegas de piedra. Asimismo, Honda es otro de los departamentos en el que los puentes atraviesan la naturaleza y hay varios edificios relevantes que retoman la historia, como la Casa Museo Alfonso López Pumarejo.

This article from AD Magazine highlights the Colombian filming locations for the upcoming Netflix series adaptation of Gabriel García Márquez's "Cien años de soledad" (One Hundred Years of Solitude). The series, directed by Laura Mora and Alex García López, premiered its first trailer on April 17. The article describes five key Colombian regions where filming took place, which serve as real-world inspiration for the fictional town of Macondo:

1. **La Guajira** - Located in northern Colombia, bordering the Caribbean Sea and Venezuela. Known for three natural parks, five native-American villages, and as the birthplace of vallenato music.

2. **Magdalena** - Named after the region's predominant river, featuring four hydrographic basins surrounded by lush nature. Notably, this is Gabriel García Márquez's birthplace.

3. **Cesar** - Particularly the capital Valledupar, known for inspiring poet Fernando Dangond's work. Features natural landscapes for camping, hiking, and ecotourism, including El Mojao with its crystal-clear waters and waterfalls.

4. **Cundinamarca** - Located near Bogotá, home to the historic Guatavita Lagoon. Offers traditional Colombian cuisine and preserved colonial architecture.

5. **Tolima** - Home to Falan, a "lost city" with 17th-century ruins from the Spanish invasion, along with Honda, featuring historic bridges and buildings like the Casa Museo Alfonso López Pumarejo.

The article also provides background on the novel's publication history: written in 18 months (1965-1966) in Mexico City, published in 1967 in Buenos Aires, and now considered a contemporary masterpiece.

## **LOS LUGARES DONDE SE GRABÓ LA SERIE “CIEN AÑOS DE SOLEDAD”**

A continuación, los lugares donde se filmó la serie “Cien años de soledad”, en la que los hijos de Gabo, Rodrigo y Gonzalo García, son los productores ejecutivos.

### **TOLIMA, COLOMBIA**

En el departamento de Tolima se grabaron varias escenas de la serie. Aquí, exactamente en cercanías de Alvarado se construyó Macondo, el cual abarcó un espacio equivalente a 70 canchas de fútbol. Las calles de esta ciudad ficticia llevan los nombres de sus seres queridos, así tenemos Papalelo, tal como García Márquez llamaba a su abuelo, el coronel Nicolás Ricardo Márquez. Asimismo, Tranquilina, como decía a su abuela materna.

Asimismo, en Ibagué se recreó la casona de la familia Buendía con una versión sorprende, pues los detalles hacen ver que estás en el mismo lugar que el escritor describe en su obra.

### **MAGDALENA**

Magdalena es el departamento de Colombia, conocida por ser la tierra natal de Gabriel García Márquez. Este departamento colombiano está conformado por cuatro cuencas hidrográficas y rodeado de naturaleza.

### **LA GUAJIRA**

Guajira está al norte de Colombia, donde viven muchos inmigrantes de países del Medio Oriente. Aquí hay tres parques naturales y cinco pueblos nativo-americanos.

### **CESAR**

El departamento de Cesar tiene hermosos paisajes naturales para realizar diversas actividades. El lugar más conocido es El Mojao.

### **CUNDINAMARCA**

Cundimarca también fue otra de las regiones donde se grabó “Cien años desoledad”. En su territorio está la laguna de Guatavita, una de las más importantes en Colombia. Se caracteriza por ser un lugar histórico muy tranquilo.

Aquí, exactamente en cercanías de Alvarado se construyó Macondo, el cual abarcó un espacio equivalente a 70 canchas de fútbol.,Magdalena es el departamento de Colombia, conocida por ser la tierra natal de Gabriel García Márquez.,La serie 'Cien años de soledad' es un ambicioso proyectos en el que participaron gran cantidad de actores y personal detrás de cámaras,Para 'Cien años de soledad' se construyeron los escenarios con apoyo de diversos profesionales como artesanos, arquitectos, historiadores y más
args.summary:
The article from El Comercio's MAG section reports on the filming locations for Netflix's adaptation of Gabriel García Márquez's "Cien años de soledad" (One Hundred Years of Solitude), directed by Laura Mora and Alex García Lopera. The 16-episode series, produced with the involvement of García Márquez's sons Rodrigo and Gonzalo García as executive producers, was filmed across multiple departments in Colombia:

- **Tolima**: The fictional town of Macondo was constructed near Alvarado, spanning an area equivalent to 70 football fields. Streets were named after family members (Papalelo for his grandfather, Tranquilina for his grandmother). The Buendía family mansion was recreated in Ibagué.
- **Magdalena**: García Márquez's birthplace, known for its four hydrographic basins and natural surroundings.
- **La Guajira**: Northern Colombia, home to three natural parks and five Native American villages, also where many Middle Eastern immigrants live.
- **Cesar**: Known for beautiful natural landscapes, particularly El Mojao.
- **Cundinamarca**: Home to the Laguna de Guatavita, a historically significant and tranquil location.

The production involved artisans, architects, historians, and other professionals in building the sets. The series is available on Netflix in two parts.
